messages:
support-ana: Heads-up: Acme reported p99 latency and intermittent 502s to the /v1/generate endpoint since ~08:15 UTC. Also seeing billing spike on their account (unexpected token consumption).

maria: Are these only in eu-west1?

support-ana: Customer in eu-west1 primarily, but also some traces from eu-central. Logs: 502s correlate with backend 'infer-worker' returning 504/ERR_IO_TIMEOUT.

kevin: We rolled cuda-driver 537 to eu fleets at 07:50 for perf fixes. @eng-oncall-tom any correlates?

eng-oncall-tom: I see storage host IO p99 increase starting 07:52 across ci-eu1-hosts. nvme qdepth spikes. Could be driver/kernel combo. Ops graph here: <link>

deploy-bot: Deployment: cuda-driver/537 rolled to eu1 at 07:50 by rollbot. Canary green.

evan: I've reproduced a p99 spike locally by hitting batch endpoint with long sequences. curl example:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" \
 -d '{"model":"gpt-large","input":"x"}' -w "\nTIME:%{time_total}\n" 
```
Got 2.8s p50 and 9.2s p99 and occasional 502s.

maria: Interesting — KV cache misses high and io wait jumps in the same time window. nvme latency logs:
```
[io] nvme0n1: qfull at qdepth=1024, svc_time p99=270ms
```

support-ana: @kevin customer also reported auth token refresh errors 401 around the same time.

kevin: 401s likely secondary due to race on token service under load. But primary is IO. Suggest immediate mitigations: route Acme to us-west hot standby, throttle long-seq jobs, and enable model fallback to quantized variant.

eng-oncall-tom: I can open emergency routing: pin acme -> usw2 for next 4h. Also increasing per-customer concurrency limit to reduce bursts.

maria: Quick mitigation steps I can run now:
- set model variant fallback: gpt-large-quant
- enable prefix caching on their customer route
- temporary disable driver 537 on 3 suspect hosts (rollback to 535)
Commands:
```
redwoodctl route update --customer acme --region usw2 --fallback-model gpt-large-quant
redwoodctl host rollback-driver --hosts host-eu1-12,host-eu1-14 --driver 535
```

kevin: :thumbsup: Do the routing first. Ops schedule for rollback needs approval.

evan: Also we should capture a repro tarball from one host before we reboot/rollback:
```
sudo journalctl -u infer-worker -o short-iso > /tmp/infer.log
sudo nvme top > /tmp/nvme.top
tar czf /tmp/repro-acme-$(date +%s).tgz /tmp/infer.log /tmp/nvme.top
```

support-ana: I've told Acme we're routing them and enabling fallback; will monitor. They're seeing billing anomalies — maybe retries inflated tokens. Can we pause billing while we investigate?

kevin: I'll ask CS to flag the account and issue credit if needed — don't change billing systems automatically. Opened ticket: TKT-8943.

eng-oncall-tom: I'll run host-side probe scripts and start rolling back driver on a canary host, and gather metrics. ETA 15m.

maria: Follow-up tasks: 1) Collect kernel and nvme stack traces 2) Bisect driver change if rollback helps 3) Long-term: kernel io-scheduling tune + limit default qdepths 4) Postmortem with mitigation playbook

opsbot: Alert created: ACME-P99-EU1-6999991234, paging oncall.

support-ana: Thanks all. Keep me posted and I'll update customer. :eyes:
